scope: evidence-based Linux and Nocturne recovery; no generated commands

entries.action: Boot normally or edit /etc/nocturne/nox-doc.conf from a root TTY so it names the desktop owner and home directory.
Do not invent a baseline. Use the minimal Nocturne Recovery login, repair manually, then create a checkpoint after one verified healthy session.
Quarantine the invalid archive. Never extract a corrupt archive or one containing absolute or parent-traversal paths.
Restore only the verified last-known-good NOC checkpoint, preserving a pre-restore archive first.
Restore the verified checkpoint. If the binary is still absent, reinstall the same signed/source NOC revision before starting the graphical target.
Keep the filesystem offline and use fsck for its exact filesystem from recovery media. NOX DOC will not force a remount or run filesystem repair automatically.
Recover space from logs or package caches with an operator present. Personal files are never selected or deleted by NOX DOC.
Reload unit metadata and clear failed state, then re-diagnose. NOX DOC does not blindly enable or restart unrelated services.
